rules: consent on paper with the purpose stated

hunt.counts_what: trackers per 250 m cell and hour of the P02 grid, cells with fewer than 10 suppressed

trenton.place: Trenton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States

hopewell.place: Hopewell, Mercer County, New Jersey, 08525, United States

duel.rule: a place counts when its nearest walk node is within 400 m of E225's nearest node along the network

destination.name: PRINCETON JCT.
destination.note: the station's stop as the rail feed places it, the same point for every mode

fill.toy astar order G: A, C, B, D, E, G

directness.note: the toolbox's directness is the straight line between two stays' centroids over the metres walked between them; the deck's number is its mean over the trips between stays at least 50 m apart, the two one-fix trips between the halves of a split queue excluded; the paper's 0.70 divides the shortest path on the path network by the metres walked

leg.chosen_because: named Silver Bullet reached from Wheeler Dealer
leg.convention: a coded row's walked_dist_m, shortest_path_m and path_directness describe the walk arriving at that stop

gravity_exp.note: gamma is the rate per km of exp(minus gamma d)

radiation.population: resident workers (RAC) of every tract, the outflow its inter-tract flows

complete.note: every ordered pair of the tracts whose centroids lie within 40 km of Nassau Hall, the internal pairs and the pairs closer than 0.5 km left out, with a zero wherever LODES lists no flow; both models fitted and scored on this one set (the old blocks scored the gravity model on the listed pairs only, and the radiation model spread part of its flow onto pairs never scored)

radii.note: half and three quarters count the unplaced commuters beyond every placed tract, exact for the half because New York's nearest point lies beyond it; nine in ten is given over the placed commuters, and with the unplaced beyond as an upper bound

park.edge_rule: fixes off the park's box are held at its edge cells

demontjoye2013.title: Unique in the Crowd: The privacy bounds of human mobility
demontjoye2013.authors: Y-A de Montjoye, C A Hidalgo, M Verleysen and V D Blondel
demontjoye2013.unique_at_2_points_note: more than half (the paper writes epsilon > .5)
demontjoye2013.quote: four spatio-temporal points are enough to uniquely identify 95% of the individuals
demontjoye2013.law: epsilon = alpha - (v h)^beta, v the antennas clustered into one cell, h the hours of one time window
demontjoye2013.decay_note: uniqueness decays approximately as the 1/10 power of the resolution (abstract, p. 1)
demontjoye2013.halving_note: each time the spatial or temporal resolution is divided by two, uniqueness falls by a constant factor of about 2^-beta (p. 3)
demontjoye2013.coarse_example: with four points, epsilon < .5 at h = 5 hours and v = 5 antennas (p. 2)

aktay2020.title: Google COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports: Anonymization Process Description (version 1.1)
aktay2020.definition: epsilon-differential privacy over adding or removing a single user's data in a single day; delta = 0 (p. 5)

levels.1: top-level subdivisions such as US states
levels.2: higher resolution such as US counties

aktay2020.epsilon_all_metrics_note: derived, not printed in the paper: 1.76 for the public places plus 0.44 residential plus 0.44 workplaces by standard composition
aktay2020.correction_2026_10_31: the deck's earlier 'budget 2.64 with noise of scale 0.44' was wrong: 0.44 is the budget of one place visit, the noise scales are 9.09 and 4.55
